The cliques are the bells and the path is the bar." width="100%"} Creates two complete graphs ("bells") of `m1` nodes each, joined by a path ("bar") of `m2` nodes. The graph has `2 * m1 + m2` nodes, and with `m2=0` the two bells are joined by a single edge. Every node on the bar, and every edge on it, is a cut point: removing it splits the graph in two. Nodes are created as the first bell, then the bar, then the second bell. The bar runs from the last node of the first bell to the first node of the second, so the numbering follows the shape from left to right; in a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Barbell graphs are a standard stress test: - community detection: two obvious clusters joined by a thin bridge - random walks and diffusion: the bar is a bottleneck, so mixing and cover times are slow - betweenness and bridge detection: all shortest paths between the bells use the bar ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [m1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each bell. Must be at least `2`. [m2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes on the bar between the bells. Must be non-negative; `m2=0` joins the bells with one edge. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m1=` is less than `2` or `m2=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two four-node bells joined by a two-node bar give `10` nodes; each bell has `6` edges and the bar adds `3` more: ::: {#45320968 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_barbell_graph(m1=4, m2=2) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (10, 15) ``` ::: ::: The bar carries every shortest path between the bells, so its two nodes, `"5"` and `"6"`, have the highest betweenness, just ahead of the bell nodes it attaches to: ::: {#20c0f204 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} scores = graph.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 2) for nid, s in scores.items() if s > 0} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'7': 0.5, '6': 0.56, '5': 0.56, '4': 0.5} ``` ::: ::: With `m2=0` the bells are joined by a single bridge edge, whose two ends are the only nodes whose removal disconnects the graph: ::: {#dd2dc7ff .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} joined = ec.Graph().add_barbell_graph(m1=3, m2=0) cut_nodes = [joined.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in joined.articulation_points()] len(joined.bridges()), cut_nodes ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, ['3', '4']) ``` ::: :::
